Subject: Developer lab: hands-on routing + load validation — 2 slot options

Hi Alex / Jamie —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To get your engineering team unblocked for the hands-on portion, we recommend a short dev lab where we:
- Walk through prompt sets and expected outputs
- Validate request routing (latency vs cost policy) with a few traffic shapes
- Run a quick load validation to confirm throughput with your expected concurrency

Two 90-minute slots that work on our side:
- Tue Dec 8, 11:00 AM PST
- Thu Dec 10, 10:00 AM PST

Agenda (draft):
1) 10 min intro + roles
2) 20 min prompt review + baseline samples
3) 30 min routing policy demo + small-scale replay
4) 25 min short load validation (2–5k tokens/min) + live metrics
5) 5 min immediate next steps / owners

Pre-reqs: a single sample dataset (10–20 prompts) and a test API key (read-only consumption) or a stub we can call. I attached a short developer_runbook_v1.pdf with the run-through and required artifacts.

If those slots don't fit, tell us three windows that do and we’ll adjust.

Best,
Sofia

Subject: Developer lab recap + action items (11 Dec session)

Team —

Thanks for running the developer lab on 11 Dec. Short recap and owners below. We hit the main checklist and captured a few follow-ups:

What we covered
- Prompt review: adjusted scoring thresholds for ambiguous intents (see prompts with prefix skyline_prompts_v2.txt)
- Routing policy: demonstrated latency-first vs cost-first routing and the automatic fallback to quantized model for long contexts
- Load validation: ran three sweeps (500, 1.5k, 3k tokens/min). Observed stable p95 latency at 280ms at 1.5k tokens/min. Full export attached (latency-results-20261211.csv).

Action items
- Alex: provide the full 1-hour traffic trace and an anonymized sample of user prompts (due 2026-12-15)
- Ben: publish the routing policy snippet we used as a Gist and share in the Drive (due 2026-12-14)
- Sofia: prepare a short comparison doc (3 slides) with cost/latency tradeoffs and recommended rollout plan for production (due 2026-12-16)
- Procurement: send PO template and initial contract questions; we can scope Dedicated capacity options if desired (requested by 2026-12-20)

Next session
- Propose a targeted follow-up: 30–45 minutes on Dec 16 to review Alex’s trace and confirm final rollout knobs. Please confirm availability.

Attachments:
- latency-results-20261211.csv (csv)
- developer_runbook_v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks again — call out if anything is missing.

Best,
